title: Stepping Stones With Reach Limit
description:
## Task

A river is crossed on a line of stones. Standing on stone `i` costs `costs[i]` (paid once, on landing; the starting stone is paid too). You start on stone 0 and must reach the last stone. From stone `i` you may jump forward to any stone from `i + 1` to `i + k`. Find the lowest possible total cost of the stones you stand on.

## Input

- `costs` — a non-empty list of non-negative integers.
- `k` — the longest allowed jump, at least 1.

## Output

The minimum total cost, including the first and last stones. Checking every allowed jump from every stone is too slow when `k` is large; a linear method is expected.

## Example

```python
cheapest_crossing([1, 3, 1, 8, 2], 2)  # returns 4
cheapest_crossing([5], 3)  # returns 5
cheapest_crossing([2, 9, 9, 9, 1], 4)  # returns 3
```

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ length of `costs` ≤ 5·10^4
- 0 ≤ each cost ≤ 10^6
- 1 ≤ `k` ≤ 5·10^4
signature: def cheapest_crossing(costs: list[int], k: int) -> int
